function: Externalises the fourth of the five 88-level lookup tables declared in the
frozen COBOL copybook app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy as classpath reference data.
The table is the set of United States state, district and territory codes
accepted when validating the state portion of a customer address.

sourceCopybookRole: The COBOL corpus under app/ is frozen and read-only. It is simultaneously
the parity oracle, the field-contract source and the traceability anchor
for this migration, so it is never edited, moved or reformatted.
parentDataItemNote: The single condition name below is an 88-level on this one two-character
parent item, so every value is exactly two characters of PIC X data.
The source line separates the name from PIC by two spaces rather than one:
a cosmetic legacy irregularity, severity Low, preserved uncorrected in the
frozen corpus because it has no effect on the field contract.
transcription: Every value is transcribed verbatim from the frozen COBOL corpus, in source
order, with no value added, removed, sorted, deduplicated, re-cased or
reformatted. A value that differs from the copybook is a parity break, not
a correction: the copybook is the sole authority.
extractionMethod: Comment-skipping literal extraction: within the inclusive line range, a
line whose first non-blank character is '*' is a COBOL comment and is
skipped; every remaining single-quoted literal is collected in source
order. Two properties of this table make fixed-column slicing unsafe, so
it is not used. First, the continuation lines are indented with one space
followed by two horizontal tabs, an indentation unique to this table among
the five - the area-code tables use two tabs with no leading space and the
state-and-zip table uses spaces alone. Second, the 88-level clause line
carries no value at all, unlike the area-code tables whose clause line
carries the first value; the first value here is on the following line.
Assuming otherwise drops the first value and shifts every index, which is
a Blocker. Extraction is verified against a whole-file total of 1276
literals across all five tables, being 490 + 410 + 80 + 56 + 240.
statementTerminator: The final source line reads 'VI'. - the trailing period closes the COBOL
statement and is not part of the value.
interiorComment: None. No comment line falls inside the value range, so no line is skipped
within it. Two comment lines bound the table and neither is data: the one
immediately above the parent item at app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy:L1011, and the
one introducing the following state-and-zip table at L1070, whose subject
is the sibling resource state-zip-prefixes.json rather than this one.
networkSources: None. Unlike the area-code tables, the copybook cites no external registry
for this table, so there is nothing to reference even historically. No
postal-service list, no ISO 3166-2:US list and no other external source
was consulted. No value is fetched, refreshed or reconciled over the
network at build time or run time, and this resource performs no outbound

observation: The comment line immediately above the parent data item describes
phone area codes. It is stale: it was left behind when the state
table was appended after the three area-code tables, and it does
disposition: Preserved, not corrected. The corpus is frozen and the comment has
no runtime effect. It is recorded here as evidence only; its text
is deliberately not carried into this resource, neither as data nor
as a description of this table.

summary: The complete set of state codes accepted by the legacy validation.
The declaration line and the first value line differ because the
88-level clause line carries no value, which is why both ranges are
Deliberately NOT in ascending code order: the sequence is
alphabetical by full state name, then the District of Columbia, then
five territories, so index 0 'AL' is immediately followed by index 1
'AK'. That ordering is source ordering and is preserved.
Composition is explanatory commentary and not a validation rule: 50
states, the District of Columbia and 5 territories. The rule the
consumer applies is membership in this array, nothing else.

invariants: The element count is exactly 56; any other count is a Blocker.
Every element is a JSON string of exactly two uppercase ASCII letters -
never a number, because the source field is PIC X(2) character data.
No element is null, empty, whitespace-padded, lower-cased or duplicated.
The order is source order. Sorting or deduplicating the array is a Medium
parity break: membership would survive but ordering would not, and
ordering is part of the transcription contract. The adjacent pairs AL->AK,
IN->IA, ME->MD, MS->MO, NE->NV->NH, NY->NC->ND, VT->VA, WA->WV->WI->WY and
WY->DC->AS hold only because the source orders by full state name; sorting
by code would destroy every one of them.
This table appears in exactly one resource. It is never merged with,
derived from, or reconciled against the other two validation resources,
and it is never duplicated as generated Java constants.
Cross-resource property, observed and intentional in the source: the
sibling resource state-zip-prefixes.json holds 240 four-character
state-and-zip combinations whose first two characters yield 62 distinct
prefixes. All 56 codes here are a subset of those 62. The 6 extra prefixes
are AA, AE and AP, which are military and diplomatic mail designations,
and FM, MH and PW, which are Freely Associated States; 56 + 6 = 62. Those
6 are valid zip-prefix combinations but are deliberately NOT accepted
state codes. Adding any of them here, or removing any of them from the
sibling, is a Blocker: it silently alters which addresses validate.

metadataHandling: This _metadata member is documentation, NOT data. The consuming service
ignores it explicitly and deliberately by its well-known name; it is never
bound as a lookup table and never participates in validation.
bindingContract: Read as UTF-8 from the classpath and bound with plain, explicitly typed
Jackson binding to string collections. No polymorphic type handling and no
default typing are used or required, and this resource carries no type
hint of any kind, so it cannot drive insecure deserialisation.
exposure: Loaded once at startup into immutable collections, so no caller can mutate
shared lookup state. A 56-element set held immutably needs no index

whatItDoes: Supplies the single table that the legacy 88-level condition name
VALID-US-STATE-CODE expressed in COBOL. A membership test against this
array replaces evaluating that condition name, and is what decides
whether the state portion of a customer address is accepted.
howToBuildAndTest: No build step: this is a static classpath resource copied verbatim into
target/classes by the standard resources phase, with no property
filtering. Build with './mvnw -B clean compile' and run the unit suite with
'./mvnw -B clean test'. The assertions for this resource live under
src/test/java/com/cardemo/unit/ and cover the element count of 56, the
first and last values AL and VI, the interior index checkpoints 14 'IA',
28 'NH' and 42 'TX', the preserved non-sorted adjacencies, and the
subset relationship against the sibling zip-prefix resource.
configurationAndDefaults: No configuration and no defaults: the content is fixed reference data and
there is no property, profile or environment variable that alters it.
The resource path itself is the only contract with the consumer.
Encoding is UTF-8 with LF line endings and two-space indentation, per the
commonFailureModesAndTroubleshooting: Resource not found on the classpath: the consumer must fail fast and
loudly rather than degrade to an empty table, because an empty table
would silently reject every customer address. Confirm the file is
present under target/classes/validation/ after a build.
Malformed content: the consumer must wrap the parse failure with this
resource path and preserve the root cause. Re-validate the file with a
strict JSON parser.
Unexpected element count: compare against the count of 56 published in
sourceTables above. A mismatch means the resource was truncated or
edited, and it is a Blocker - re-derive it from app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy.
A state code rejected that the legacy system accepted: verify the value
against the copybook line range, never against any external list. The
usual cause is an extractor that sliced fixed columns, split on the
horizontal tabs, or treated the 88-level clause line as carrying the
first value and so lost 'AL'.
Ordering reported as wrong because the array is not alphabetical by
code: that is expected and correct. Do not sort it.
A privacy note for the consumer rather than for this file: a state code
is a fragment of a customer address, so the value being looked up must
never be written to a log line.

designRationale: This table is data, not code. Generating it as Java constants would put
reference data into a compilation unit, make the count harder to audit and
add source that no compiler check makes safer - and across the five tables
of this copybook it would run to well over a thousand lines. Externalising
it as a classpath resource keeps the membership exactly auditable against
the copybook, keeps the count visible for verification, and is the
notAvailable: Any documented rationale in the source for why AA, AE, AP, FM, MH and PW
are valid zip-prefix combinations yet are not accepted state codes:
Not available. The copybook declares both sets and documents no rule, and
no postal or territorial specification exists anywhere in this repository,
so no behaviour is inferred from the difference and the asymmetry is
reproduced rather than reconciled. To resolve it, what is needed is an
authoritative statement of the rule from the system owner, or a postal
specification admitted into the repository as a reference artefact.
A lookup latency or throughput objective:
Not available. The legacy source publishes no service level of any kind,
so none is invented here; the performance gate records a measured baseline
rather than a target. To set one, what is needed is a stated objective
from the system owner, which no artefact in this repository supplies.
